readings.title: The Command to Leave Horeb
readings.subtitle: Moses Recounts the Journey
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 1:1] These are the words which Mosheh spoke to all Yisra’ěl beyond the Yarděn in the wilderness, in the desert plain opposite Suph, between Paran and Tophel, and Laḇan, and Ḥatsěroth, and Di Zahaḇ, [2] eleven days’ journey from Ḥorěḇ by way of Mount Sě‛ir to Qaḏěsh Barněa. [3] And it came to be in the fortieth year, in the eleventh new moon, on the first day of the new moon, that Mosheh spoke to the children of Yisra’ěl according to all that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded <dn>את</dn> <dn>him</dn> concerning them, [4] after he had stricken <dn>את</dn> Siḥon sovereign of the Amorites, who dwelt in Ḥeshbon, and <dn>את</dn> Oḡ sovereign of Bashan, who dwelt at Ashtaroth in Eḏre‛i. [5] Beyond the Yarděn, in the land of Mo’aḇ, Mosheh undertook to declare <dn>את</dn> this Torah, saying, [6] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> spoke to us in Ḥorěḇ, saying, <dq>‘You have dwelt long enough at this mountain.</dq> [7] <dq>Turn and set out on your way, and go into the mountains of the Amorites, and to all the neighbouring places in the desert plain, in the mountains and in the low country, and in the Negeḇ and on the seacoast, to the land of the Kena‛anites and to Leḇanon, as far as the great river, the River Euphrates.</dq> [8] <dq>See, <dn>I</dn> have set <dn>את</dn> the land before you. Go in and possess the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> swore to your fathers, to Aḇraham, to Yitsḥaq, and to Ya‛aqoḇ, to give to them and their seed after them.’</dq>”

readings.title: The Appointment of Leaders
readings.subtitle: Sharing the Burden of Israel
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 1:9] “And I spoke to you at that time, saying, ‘I am unable to bear you by myself. [10] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has increased you, and see, you are today as numerous as the stars of the heavens. [11] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of your fathers is going to add to you a thousand times more than you are, and bless you as <dn>He</dn> has spoken to you! [12] How do I bear your pressure and your burden and your strife, by myself? [13] Choose men, wise and understanding, and known to your tribes, and let me appoint them as your heads.’ [14] “And you answered me and said, ‘The word which you have spoken to us to do is good.’ [15] “And I took <dn>את</dn> the heads of your tribes, wise men and known, and made them heads over you, leaders of thousands, and leaders of hundreds, and leaders of fifties, and leaders of tens, and officers for your tribes. [16] “And I commanded <dn>את</dn> your judges at that time, saying, ‘When hearing between your brothers, judge righteously between a man and his brother or the stranger who is with him. [17] Do not show partiality in right-ruling, hear the small as well as the great. Do not be afraid of anyone’s face, for the right-ruling belongs to <dn>Elohim</dn>. And the case which is too hard for you, bring it to me, and I shall hear it.’ [18] “And I commanded <dn>את</dn> you at that time <dn>את</dn> all the words which you should do.

readings.title: Spies Sent into Canaan
readings.subtitle: The Goodness of the Promised Land
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 1:19] “Then we set out from Ḥorěḇ, and went through <dn>את</dn> all that great and awesome wilderness which you saw on the way to the mountains of the Amorites, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> had commanded us. And we came to Qaḏěsh Barněa. [20] “And I said to you, ‘You have come to the mountains of the Amorites, which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving us. [21] See, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has set <dn>את</dn> the land before you. Go up and possess it, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of your fathers has spoken to you. Do not fear, nor be discouraged.’ [22] “And all of you came near to me and said, ‘Let us send men before us, and let them search out <dn>את</dn> the land for us, and bring back word to us of <dn>את</dn> the way by which we should go up, and of <dn>את</dn> the cities into which we would come.’ [23] “And the matter was good in my eyes, so I took twelve of your men, one man from each tribe. [24] “And they turned and went up into the mountains, and came to the wadi Eshkol, and spied it out. [25] “And they took some of the fruit of the land in their hands and brought it down to us. And they brought back word to us, saying, ‘The land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving us is good.’

readings.title: Israel's Rebellion and Defeat
readings.subtitle: The Consequence of Unbelief
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 1:26] “But you would not go up and rebelled against the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, [27] and grumbled in your tents, and said, ‘Because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was hating <dn>את</dn> us, <dn>He</dn> has brought us out of the land of Mitsrayim to give us into the hand of the Amorites, to destroy us. [28] Where are we going to? Our brothers have made our hearts melt, saying, “The people are greater and taller than we, the cities are great and walled up to the heavens, and we saw the sons of the Anaqim there too.” ’ [29] “Then I said to you, ‘Have no dread or fear of them. [30] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, who is going before you, <dn>He</dn> does fight for you, according to all <dn>He</dn> did for <dn>את</dn> you in Mitsrayim before your eyes, [31] and in the wilderness, where you saw how <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has borne you, as a man bears his son, in all the way that you went until you came to this place.’ [32] “Yet in this matter you are putting no trust in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, [33] who is going before you in the way to seek out a place for you to pitch your tents, to show you the way you should go, in fire by night and in a cloud by day. [34] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> heard <dn>את</dn> the voice of your words, and was wroth, and took an oath, saying, [35] <dq>‘Not one of these men of this evil generation shall see that good land of which <dn>I</dn> swore to give to your fathers,</dq> [36] <dq>except Kalěḇ son of Yephunneh. He shall see it, and to him and his children <dn>I</dn> give <dn>את</dn> the land on which he walked, because he followed <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> completely.’</dq> [37] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was enraged with me for your sakes, saying, <dq>‘You do not go in there, either.</dq> [38] <dq>Yehoshua the son of Nun, who stands before you, he shall go in there. Strengthen him, for he shall cause <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl to inherit.</dq> [39] <dq>And your little ones and your children, who you say are for a prey, who today have no knowledge of good and evil, they are going in there. And to them <dn>I</dn> give it, and they are to possess it.</dq> [40] <dq>But you, turn and take your journey into the wilderness by the Way of the Sea of Reeds.’</dq> [41] “Then you answered and said to me, ‘We have sinned against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. We ourselves are going up, and we shall fight, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> commanded us.’ And when each one of you had girded on his battle gear, you were ready to go up into the mountain. [42] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, <dq>‘Say to them, “Do not go up nor fight, for <dn>I</dn> am not in your midst, lest you be smitten before your enemies.” ’</dq> [43] “So I spoke to you, but you would not listen and rebelled against the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and acted proudly, and went up into the mountain. [44] “Then the Amorites who dwelt in that mountain came out against you and chased you as bees do, and drove you back from Sě‛ir to Ḥormah. [45] “And you returned and wept before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, but <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> would not listen to your voice nor give ear to you. [46] “So you dwelt in Qaḏěsh many days, according to the days that you dwelt.

readings.title: The Journey Around Edom and Moab
readings.subtitle: Respecting the Borders of Esau and Lot
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 2:1] “Then we turned and set out into the wilderness, the way of the Sea of Reeds, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to me, and we went round Mount Sě‛ir, many days. [2] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to me, saying, [3] <dq>‘You have gone around this mountain long enough, turn northward.</dq> [4] <dq>And command <dn>את</dn> the people, saying, “You are about to pass over into the border of your brothers, the descendants of Ěsav, who live in Sě‛ir, and they are afraid of you. So be on your guard.</dq> [5] <dq>“Do not strive with them, for <dn>I</dn> do not give you any of their land, no, not so much as one footstep, because <dn>I</dn> have given Mount Sě‛ir to Ěsav as a possession.</dq> [6] <dq>“What food you buy from them with silver you shall eat. And also, what water you buy from them with silver you shall drink.</dq> [7] <dq>“For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has blessed you in all the work of your hand. <dn>He</dn> has known your wandering through <dn>את</dn> this great wilderness. These forty years <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has been with you, you have not lacked any matter.” ’</dq> [8] “And when we passed beyond our brothers, the descendants of Ěsav who dwell in Sě‛ir, away from the way of the desert plain, away from Ěylath and Etsyon Geḇer, we turned and passed over by way of the Wilderness of Mo’aḇ. [9] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, <dq>‘Do not distress Mo’aḇ, nor stir yourself up against them in battle, for <dn>I</dn> do not give you any of their land as a possession, because <dn>I</dn> have given Ar to the descendants of Lot as a possession.’</dq> ” [10] (The Ěmites had dwelt there formerly, a people as great and numerous and tall as the Anaqim. [11] They were also reckoned as Repha’ites, like the Anaqim, but the Mo’aḇites call them Ěmites. [12] And the Ḥorites formerly dwelt in Sě‛ir, but the descendants of Ěsav dispossessed them and destroyed them from before them, and dwelt in their place, as Yisra’ěl did to the land of their possession which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave them.) [13] <dq>“ ‘Now rise up, and pass over <dn>את</dn> the wadi Zereḏ.’</dq> So we passed over <dn>את</dn> the wadi Zereḏ. [14] “And the time we took to come from Qaḏěsh Barněa until we passed over the wadi Zereḏ was thirty-eight years, until all the generation of the men of battle was consumed from the midst of the camp, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had sworn to them. [15] “And also, the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was against them, to destroy them from the midst of the camp until they were consumed. [16] “And it came to be, when all the men of battle had finally perished from among the people, [17] that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to me, saying, [18] <dq>‘This day you are to pass over at <dn>את</dn> Ar, <dn>את</dn> the boundary of Mo’aḇ.</dq> [19] <dq>And when you come near the children of Ammon, do not distress them nor stir yourself up against them, for <dn>I</dn> do not give you any of the land of the children of Ammon as a possession, because <dn>I</dn> have given it to the descendants of Lot as a possession.’</dq> [20] (That was also reckoned as a land of Repha’ites. Repha’ites formerly dwelt there. But the Ammonites call them Zamzummim, [21] a people as great and numerous and tall as the Anaqim. But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> destroyed them before them, and they dispossessed them and dwelt in their place, [22] as <dn>He</dn> had done for the descendants of Ěsav, who dwelt in Sě‛ir, when <dn>He</dn> destroyed <dn>את</dn> the Ḥorites from before them. They dispossessed them and dwelt in their place, even to this day. [23] And the Avvim who dwelt in villages as far as Azzah, the Kaphtorim who came from Kaphtor, destroyed them and dwelt in their place). [24] <dq>‘Arise, set out and pass over <dn>את</dn> the wadi Arnon. See, <dn>I</dn> have given into your hand <dn>את</dn> Siḥon the Amorite, sovereign of Ḥeshbon, and <dn>את</dn> his land. Begin to possess it, and stir up yourself against him in battle.</dq> [25] <dq>This day <dn>I</dn> begin to put the dread and fear of you upon the peoples under all the heavens, who, when they hear the report of you, shall tremble and shake because of you.’</dq>

readings.title: The Defeat of Sihon
readings.subtitle: Israel Conquers Heshbon
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 2:26] “Then I sent messengers from the Wilderness of Qeḏěmoth to Siḥon sovereign of Ḥeshbon, with words of peace, saying, [27] ‘Let me pass over through your land on the highway. I shall go on the highway and turn neither to the right nor to the left. [28] What food you sell me for silver I shall eat, and what water you give me for silver I shall drink. Only let me pass over on foot, [29] as the descendants of Ěsav who dwell in Sě‛ir and the Mo’aḇites who dwell in Ar did for me – until I pass over the Yarděn to the land <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving us.’ [30] “But Siḥon sovereign of Ḥeshbon would not let us pass over, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> hardened <dn>את</dn> his spirit and strengthened <dn>את</dn> his heart, to give him into your hand, as it is this day. [31] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, <dq>‘See, <dn>I</dn> have begun to give <dn>את</dn> Siḥon and <dn>את</dn> his land over to you. Begin to possess – in order to possess his land.’</dq> [32] “And Siḥon and all his people came out against us to fight at Yahats, [33] and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> gave him over to us, so we struck <dn>את</dn> him, and <dn>את</dn> his sons, and <dn>את</dn> all his people. [34] “And we took <dn>את</dn> all his cities at that time, and we put <dn>את</dn> the men, women, and little ones of every city under the ban, we left none remaining. [35] “Only the livestock we took as plunder for ourselves, and the spoil of the cities which we captured. [36] “From Aro‛ěr, which is on the edge of the wadi Arnon, and the city that is by the wadi, as far as Gil‛aḏ, there was not one city too high for us. <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> gave <dn>את</dn> all to us. [37] “Only you did not go near the land of the children of Ammon – anywhere along the wadi Yabboq, or to the cities of the mountains, or anywhere as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> commanded us.

readings.title: The Defeat of Og
readings.subtitle: Israel Conquers Bashan
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 3:1] “Then we turned and went up the way to Bashan. And Oḡ sovereign of Bashan came out against us, he and all his people, to battle at Eḏre‛i. [2] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, <dq>‘Do not fear him, for <dn>I</dn> have given <dn>את</dn> him and <dn>את</dn> all his people and <dn>את</dn> his land into your hand. And you shall do to him as you did to Siḥon sovereign of the Amorites, who dwelt at Ḥeshbon.’</dq> [3] “So <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> also gave into our hands <dn>את</dn> Oḡ sovereign of Bashan, with <dn>את</dn> all his people, and we struck him until he had no survivors remaining. [4] “And we captured <dn>את</dn> all his cities at that time. There was not a city which we did not take from them: sixty cities, all the district of Argoḇ, the reign of Oḡ in Bashan. [5] “All these cities were fenced with high walls, gates and bars, besides a great many unwalled towns. [6] “And we put <dn>את</dn> them under the ban, as we did to Siḥon sovereign of Ḥeshbon, putting the men, the women, and the children of every city under the ban. [7] “But all the livestock and the spoil of the cities we took as booty for ourselves. [8] “And at that time we took <dn>את</dn> the land, from the hand of the two sovereigns of the Amorites, that was beyond the Yarděn, from the wadi Arnon to Mount Ḥermon [9] “(Tsiḏonians call Ḥermon, Siryon – and the Amorites call it Senir), [10] all the cities of the plain, all Gil‛aḏ, and all Bashan, as far as Salḵah and Eḏre‛i, cities of the reign of Oḡ in Bashan. [11] “For only Oḡ sovereign of Bashan was left of the remnant of the Repha’ites. See, his bedstead was an iron bedstead. Is it not in Rabbah of the children of Ammon? Nine cubits is its length and four cubits its width, according to the cubit of a man.

readings.title: The Division of the Land
readings.subtitle: Reuben, Gad, and Half-Manasseh Inherit
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 3:12] “And <dn>את</dn> this land, which we possessed at that time, from Aro‛ěr, which is by the wadi Arnon, and half the mountains of Gil‛aḏ and its cities, I gave to the Re’uḇěnites and the Gaḏites. [13] “And the rest of Gil‛aḏ, and all Bashan, the reign of Oḡ, I gave to half the tribe of Menashsheh – all the district of Argoḇ, with all Bashan, called the land of the Repha’ites. [14] “Ya‛ir son of Menashsheh had taken <dn>את</dn> all the district of Argoḇ, as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Ma‛aḵathites, and called <dn>את</dn> them after his own name: <dn>את</dn> the Bashan of Havoth Ya‛ir, to this day. [15] “And to Maḵir I gave Gil‛aḏ. [16] “And to the Re’uḇěnites and the Gaḏites I gave from Gil‛aḏ as far as the wadi Arnon, the middle of the wadi as the border, as far as the wadi Yabboq, the border of the children of Ammon, [17] and the desert plain, with the Yarděn as the border, from Kinnereth as far as the Sea of the Araḇah, the Salt Sea, below the slopes of Pisgah on the east. [18] “And I commanded <dn>את</dn> you at that time, saying, ‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has given you <dn>את</dn> this land to possess. All you sons of might, pass over armed before your brothers, the children of Yisra’ěl. [19] But let your wives and your little ones, and your livestock – I know that you have much livestock – stay in your cities which I have given you, [20] until <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has given rest to your brothers as to you, and they also possess <dn>את</dn> the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving them beyond the Yarděn. Then you shall return, each man to his possession which I have given you.’

readings.title: Moses Forbidden to Cross the Jordan
readings.subtitle: Joshua Commissioned to Lead
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 3:21] “And I commanded <dn>את</dn> Yehoshua at that time, saying, ‘Your eyes have seen <dn>את</dn> all that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has done to these two sovereigns. <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does the same to all the reigns which you are passing over. [22] Do not fear them, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> <dn>Himself</dn> fights for you.’ [23] “And I pleaded with <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> at that time, saying, [24] ‘O Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, You have begun to show <dn>את</dn> Your servant <dn>את</dn> Your greatness and <dn>את</dn> Your strong hand, for who is a mighty one in the heavens or on earth who does according to Your works and according to Your might? [25] I pray, let me pass over and see <dn>את</dn> the good land beyond the Yarděn, this good hill country, and Leḇanon.’ [26] “But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was enraged with me, for your sake, and would not listen to me, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, <dq>‘Enough of that! Speak no more to <dn>Me</dn> about this matter.</dq> [27] <dq>Go up to the top of Pisgah, and lift up your eyes westward, and northward, and southward, and eastward, and look with your eyes, for you do not pass over this Yarděn.</dq> [28] <dq>But command <dn>את</dn> Yehoshua, and strengthen him and make him brave, for he shall pass over before this people and cause them to inherit <dn>את</dn> the land which you see.’</dq> [29] “And we dwelt in the valley opposite Běyth Pe‛or.
